chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: Hello and welcome to this video lecture series on microprocessor and microcontroller.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: And we are currently studying the 8086 microprocessor. And this is 18th video

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: lecture in the complete series and 8th video lecture for 8086 microprocessor. In the previous

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: video, we have studied the minimum mode of operation of 8086 microprocessor. And by minimum

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: mode of operation, we mean that in the complete circuit, we will only have one microprocessor,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: which will be 8086. Rest all will be peripherals or externally interfaced memory. So that way,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: if we make our microcomputer system, that system will be called as in minimum mode of operation.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: Similarly, there is an other mode in which various other processors can also be coupled with this

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: 8086 microprocessor. And that mode is called as maximum mode of 8086 microprocessor. So maximum

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: mode, as we have also discussed earlier, is used to interface several other things like 8087 math

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: coprocessor. Then there is an input output processor, etc, which we are going to see. So there are various

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: things which can be coupled with this 8086 microprocessor to enhance the capability of the

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: complete circuit that we have constructed, right. So before beginning, let me just show you some slides

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: for the pin diagram, where we will first again, distinguish between the maximum and minimum mode

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: of operation in terms of the pins that will be used. So here you see the pin diagram of 8086 microprocessor.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: And to be able to operate this microprocessor in maximum or minimum mode, as we have already

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: discussed, that the pin number 33 has to be set or reset accordingly, right. So if the value at this

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: pin is 1, then it is operating in minimum mode of operation, that means a single processor mode of

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: operation, or otherwise, if it is 0, then it is operating in the maximum mode of operation or

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: multiprocessor mode of operation, right. And all of the pins will have same meaning for both of the

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: modes, except for the pins that you see from pin number 31 to pin number 24, I mean 24 to 31, right.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: So whatever is written inside these small brackets, it is applicable for your minimum mode of operation.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: And we have discussed this in the previous lecture together with the timing diagram.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: And the same thing we are going to do for this maximum mode of operation, where this request,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: comma, grant pin will be used rq slash gt 0, and this request slash grant pin 1. So this is used by the

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: external devices like external microprocessors or external peripheral to gain the control of this 8086

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: system and internal buses, etc. So in that case, the priority will be given to request grant 0.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: In case there are two occurrences of requests from various devices, then in that case, the priority

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: will be first given to rq slash gt 0. And after that, rq slash gt bar with 1 will be served, right.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: Then we have lock pin, we have understood the meaning of lock pin, when microprocessor 8086

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: is not willing to give the control of its internal buses to the external world, then the lock pin

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: will be floated high. And this will be known to the external world through this status pin.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: Then this S0, S1 and S2, these are the status pins which this microprocessor has. And according to this

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: S0, S1 and S2 status, this microprocessor will be performing the input output read or memory read,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: input output write or input output write or input output write or input output write cycle. So the

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: status of this S0, S1 and S2 will let us know that. So let us first have a look at those relevant S0 bar,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: S1 bar and S2 bar status pins. So here you see that for various combinations, we have these values

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: input output port, write input output port, then halt instruction fetch, read memory, write memory and

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: passing inactive. So we have already discussed this in one of our lectures, the meaning of these

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: relevant status pins. So these status pins will be used here. Then this QS0 and QS1, we have already

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: said that this QS0 and QS1 will be used with your status of your queue, I mean instruction queue that is

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: there in microprocessor. So I think that those slides are also there. So let me just bring those

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: relevant slides. Yeah. So this QS0 and QS1, it tells you the status of the six byte instruction queue that

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: we have seen in the architecture of 8086. So for 00, there is no operation which is performed on queue in

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: the last executed instruction. For 01, the first byte has been taken by the last instruction. For 10,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: the queue has to be amputed. And for 11, you have to access the subsequent byte, right? So this is

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: what we mean by these pins and they can be used in this maximum mode of operation. So we will see that

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: in current lecture, we will see the operation of maximum mode and we will find it highly similar to

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: minimum mode with some differences in the hardware implementation, right? So these control signals,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: sorry, the status signals that you see here, S0, S1 and S2, they will be applied to one IC and that IC

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: will be generating the control signals for the external world. I mean how this 8086 microprocessor

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: will deal with the external world. So those are all the things that we are going to see in current

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: lecture. And let me first again show you what we did on the last 10. So this was this minimum mode

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: system which we studied on the last 10. And we saw that to be able to operate a microprocessor,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: we first need to have a clock, clock 8284 IC. So this 8284 IC is the clock generator IC. And we saw that

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: the pins that we had an output from this IC are connected to the clock ready and reset. And these,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: all of these were at different frequencies, right? So the work of 8284 IC here is to just simply,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: you know, provide the appropriate frequency to the appropriate signals. And we had this PCLK output

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: from here also, which was for peripheral clock. It is not shown here, but it can be used, right?

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: Then after applying this clock, we had these latches because we saw that in T1 state, in T1 timing diagram

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: state, we have to latch the addresses. So for that, since the addresses in 8086 are of this 20,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: they are of 20 bits. So that is why we need to have these three such latches here because individual

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: latches will be having a capability of eight bits or one byte. So we had these three latches.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: And so 20 bits out of those complete available 24 storing capacity will be used there. And then there

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: was a trans receiver. This was an optional device, but more or less it is used with this microprocessor

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: because it is used to strengthen the signal that we have received from here. And since multiple devices

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: are interfaced with this microprocessor, so they can all draw their signal from this trans receiver.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: Then we have odd and even memory bank of addresses, which are connected of this storage, externally stored,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: external memory are connected. And then input output devices were there together with their address selection

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: logic. And regarding the timing diagram of this minimum mode, what we have studied was

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: this for the minimum mode of operation, as we can see here, let me just show you the relevant slides

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: here first. So this is for the minimum mode of operation. So if you can see for minimum mode of

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: operation in T1 state, the main purpose is ALE has to be enabled. And that will enable the 8282 latches

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: and 8282 will latch the addresses. So in the first timing state or first P state, the main purpose that

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: happens is the address that has been floated on the address bus is latched onto the external 8282 latch.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: Then in T2 state, what the main purpose is that this DEN signal has to be enabled. DEN is lowered.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: DEN bar is lowered means DEN is enabled so that the trans receiver can be enabled. And the appropriate

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: signals of read and light have to be activated. Whatever we want to perform, they have to be

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: activated or deactivated. Hence, sorry, activated, not deactivated. Hence, this AD0 to AD15 go through

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: high impedance state. So when you have activated these signals, then in that case, this AD0 to AD15

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: won't have any meaning and they will go to high impedance state. In T3 state, the actual data transfer

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: happens and insertion of additional weight states in between T3 and T4 if it is required. If the device

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: which is externally interseased is slow, then in that case, this is required. And in the T4 state,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: what happens is you clear the signals basically. Whatever signals have been set for a particular

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: operation. So DEN bar will be raised high so that your trans receiver IC will be deactivated. Then read

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: write signal will be raised high, not read write, read write bar signal will be raised high so that

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: they are deactivated. And for the next T1 state, you will be setting the memory or the input output

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: signal so that you can do it accordingly. So in today's lecture, we will see that for

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: maximum mode of operation, this all will be valid, but there are some changes in the hardware. So it

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: will be all of this thing will be achieved through a different set of hardware. So I will show you

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: this chart for this maximum mode also as of now. So this is the chart for maximum mode. We will

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: discuss it once we discuss the hardware part, but we will see that most of the things are similar

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: here. ALE is enabled in first T state and addresses are lashed. Then this DEN bar is set as zero. And

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: then the data transfer actually happens in T3 and additional T states are introduced if it is

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: required if the peripheral device is slow. And then in T4 state, you have to finally deactivate your

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: signals. Essentially the same operations happen in that mode also, in maximum mode also, but they are

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: achieved through different hardware. So the signals that you notice here, AMWC bar, AIOWC bar, etc.

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: I will make the meaning of all of these clear. And then we will come to the slide again.

chunks.text: So let me just go on to this maximum mode operation of 8086. So you see here, this is not the complete

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: So to begin with, this is a good start. So let us see. So here you have got this 8086 CPU. So this

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: is your 8086 CPU. And this is the diagram for maximum mode of operation. So obviously, if it is operating

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: in maximum mode at the maximum or minimum pin, you need to ground that signal because MX bar or the

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: maximum mode will be on when you have ground here. In the earlier case, if you see in the earlier case,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: when we were using minimum mode, we have applied VCC here. VCC corresponds to positive logic. I mean,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: logic value one and this ground correspond to logic value zero. So since we want to operate this in

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: maximum mode, so the first thing that we will do is we have to apply a ground signal here, which is

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: logic level zero value. After that, we have to apply this clock, which is 8284 clock generator,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: and it will be applied in the exact same way as we have done for minimum mode of operation. So

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: this clock is independent of maximum or minimum mode of operation. So I am not discussing it in

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: detail further. The explanation remains the same. Now, looking at the two old ICs, which are familiar to us,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: which are 8282 latch and 8286 trans receiver, right? So these two are the old familiar ICs that have

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: been come from minimum mode again. But now this time, they are not directly controlled by the

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: microprocessor. However, they are actually controlled by this 8288 bus controller, right? So this is a new

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: device that has been introduced here, which is called as 8288 bus controller. So this 8288 bus

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: controller, it actually takes the status signals S0, S1 and S2 from this microprocessor 8086,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: and it converts them into appropriate memory read, memory write operations, etc. here, right? Because in the

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: table we have seen in the table for statuses of S0 bar, S1 bar and S2 bar, what we have seen was the

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: for different eight values of these S0, S1 and S2, different operations were performed. So this 8288

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: Intel bus controller IC will actually do the same job for you. It will generate the appropriate

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: signals, right? So let me just discuss the relevant outputs of this 8288 bus controller. So the inputs are

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: these and the outputs you can see here, MRDC. MRDC means M for memory, RD for read and C for your

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: command, memory read command. So this is memory read command, MRDC. Similarly, MWTC, this is called as

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: memory write command, right? So all of these are active low signals. So memory read command, memory write

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: command, then you have advanced memory write command. And correspondingly, you have advanced

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: input output write command, right? So these two are similar signals as advanced memory write command

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: and advanced input output write command. So why do we call them advanced? So the reason is if you have

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: a slow peripheral, which is interfaced with this microprocessor, then that peripheral, if you want

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: to write something onto that peripheral, we will be providing signals through these two pins, AMWC bar

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: and AIUWC bar, which is advanced memory write command and advanced input output write command,

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: so that it gets additional one clock cycle for getting prepared, right? So when you provide them

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: these two, when you provide them signals at these two pins, whether it is externally interfaced memory or

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: input output signal, so if that is slow, then in that case, through these signals, if you provide the

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: output to those inputs or to those devices, then it will get an additional T state to get prepared for

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: that transfer. However, you can see that you have signals like IOWC, which is input output write command

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: and IOWC is input output write command. And there is an advanced version of this. So IOWC, you do not get

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: any additional T state for getting prepared for transfer of data. Because if you provide output

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: through this particular pin, then in that case, it is assumed that your input output device is fast enough

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: to catch up with this, right? So that is the difference between advanced mode and normal mode. So IOWC is already

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: there. And you can see that IORC, that is input output read bar, it is also there, right? And INTA bar

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: stands for interrupt acknowledge. And we very well know what is the purpose of that. If any interrupt

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: appears here, and if the interrupt flag is set inside microprocessor, and if it is a

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: non-maskable instruction, then it is accepted and it is acknowledged at this particular pin. If it is

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: a maskable instruction or a non-maskable instruction, if interrupt flag is set INTA bar through it will be

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: acknowledged. But if interrupt flag is 0, then for maskable interrupts, the interrupt will not be

chunks.title: Video 18 - MAX mode of 8086
chunks.text: acknowledged and INTA bar pin will not be appropriately set. So this is the meaning of all of these pins.

chunks.text: And if you notice here, there are certain outputs which are called as DEN, DT slash Q, and ALE. So they all

chunks.text: Yeah. So if you see this thing here, so this ALE, etc, DEN bar, etc, they were all valid for this
